events.text: E4 class locomotives introduced, larger version of E3 class.

evidence.quote: They were introduced in 1897

events.text: Brighton Works began building the class (75 locomotives).

evidence.quote: Seventy-five members of the class were built by Brighton Works between December 1897 and September 1903

events.text: Brighton Works finished building the class.

evidence.quote: Seventy-five members of the class were built by Brighton Works between December 1897 and September 1903

events.text: Four locomotives rebuilt by D. E. Marsh and designated E4X.

evidence.quote: In 1909 , four locomotives were rebuilt by D . E . Marsh with larger boilers and designated E4X

events.label: deployment
events.text: Class members first worked at an ammunition dump in Audruicq, France.

evidence.quote: They first worked at an ammunition dump in Audruicq , France in November 1917

events.label: deployment
events.text: Class members sent to the Arras area, France.

evidence.quote: to the Arras area in February 1918

events.text: All class members returned to England from France.

evidence.quote: All of them were returned to England in 1919

events.text: Class entered Southern Railway ownership.

evidence.quote: All of the class survived to enter Southern Railway ownership in 1923

events.label: air raid
events.text: No. 2483 Hellingly severely damaged by enemy action at Eastbourne motive power depot during the Baedeker Blitz

evidence.quote: No . 2483 Hellingly , was severely damaged as a result of enemy action against Eastbourne motive power depot in 1942

events.label: scrapped
events.text: Hellingly scrapped

evidence.quote: Hellingly was scrapped in July 1944

events.label: trial
events.text: No. 2510 tested unsuccessfully on the Isle of Wight railways

evidence.quote: No . 2510 , was tested on the railways of the Isle of Wright in 1947

events.text: Class passed to British Railways with Southern Railway nationalisation.

evidence.quote: following the nationalisation of the Southern Railway as part of British Railways in 1948

events.label: withdrawal
events.text: Class withdrawals from service commenced.

evidence.quote: withdrawals commenced in 1955

events.label: withdrawal
events.text: Most of the class withdrawn, from 1958.

evidence.quote: Most of the class were withdrawn between 1958 and 1964

events.label: withdrawal
events.text: Most of the class withdrawals ended.

evidence.quote: Most of the class were withdrawn between 1958 and 1964

events.label: preserved No. 32473
events.text: Preserved No. 32473 withdrawn from traffic and dismantled

evidence.quote: The engine was withdrawn from traffic in 1971 and dismantled

events.label: preserved No. 32473
events.text: Preserved No. 32473 returned to traffic after a long overhaul

evidence.quote: following a long overhaul , she returned to traffic in 1997

events.label: preserved No. 32473
events.text: Preserved No. 32473 repainted into British Railways lined black mixed traffic livery

evidence.quote: In 2005 she was repainted into British Railways lined black mixed traffic livery

events.label: preserved No. 32473
events.text: Preserved No. 32473 withdrawn from service and taken into the Bluebell workshops for overhaul

evidence.quote: Following withdrawal from service in May 2008

events.label: preserved No. 32473
events.text: Overhaul and repaint into 1920s Southern Railway green completed

evidence.quote: This was completed during January 2010

undated_mentions: During World War I, members borrowed by the Railway Operating Division for work in France
After Grouping, class mainly found around the Central section of the Southern Railway
Later in British Railways days, several used as station pilots, including at London Waterloo
